changelog: Fix: v3.14.5's 0.5% relative tolerance on entry_price was itself wrong -- a real full-account run with it already in place still returned 15 'needs attention' rows spanning 0.9% off (ADA 0.1816 vs stored 0.1800) to 100% off (PUMP 0.004412 vs stored 0.0000), a range no single percentage threshold can cover because it isn't proportional rounding. Checked the actual stored values against the incoming ones: every discrepancy is reproduced exactly by truncating (not rounding) the incoming price to 2 decimal places -- confirmed by JUP (0.189 rounds to 0.19, which would not match the stored 0.1800, but truncates to 0.18, which matches exactly). The originally-specified fix formula (ROUND(incoming,4)=stored) was checked against these same examples before writing any SQL and matched none of them; shipped TRUNCATE(incoming,2)=stored instead, which matches all four

Change: BitfundedImportController::matchAll()'s entry_price condition is now 'entry_price = ? OR TRUNCATE(?, 2) = entry_price OR entry_price = 0' -- exact equality (keeps a re-paste of already-correct rows idempotent, since a truncation-only check would itself break that), truncated-to-2-decimals equality (the confirmed legacy hand-transcription mechanism), or stored value is exactly 0 (its own case, not a tolerance -- a pre-v3.14.5 DECIMAL(14,4) column could truncate a genuinely sub-cent price to nothing, and no comparison against a destroyed value is meaningful, so the match is accepted on pair/direction/time/pnl alone). This resolves the PUMP rows without the manual follow-up v3.14.5 predicted they'd need. entry_price is a consistency check now, not a percentage tolerance; a genuinely different trade at the same timestamp still fails to match since pair, direction, the time window, and pnl within a cent all still have to agree simultaneously. ENTRY_PRICE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_PCT removed, no longer used
